newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi says inflation now 2.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi says inflation now 2.4 percent.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Monday Italian inflation was running at 2.4 percent.
Ciampi told a news conference that when the 1997 average inflation target of 2.5 percent was set, people were sceptical, "even within the government." But he said "now, we are at 2.4 percent."
Eleven Italian cities released preliminary February inflation data on Thursday and Friday that pointed to year-on-year inflation of 2.2 percent, a fall of 0.1 percent month-on-month.
That data accounted for cuts in electricity tariffs. If the price cuts had not been factored in, officials said inflation would be between 2.3 and 2.4 percent year-on-year.
The National Statistics Office, ISTAT, will release official February inflation data on March 4.
